mainTopic: Honest תלמידי חכמים and returning lost items by recognition (טביעות עין), a story about מר זוטרא חסידא, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's concession about new vessels that must be announced
overview: The amud opens by finishing שמואל's list of three things a תלמיד חכם may change his words about: his learning, his bed, and his host. מר זוטרא explains why it matters: such a scholar is trusted to claim a lost item just by recognizing it (טביעות עין). A short story shows מר זוטרא חסידא catching a thief by watching how a student treated someone else's cloak. A ברייתא then teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees that new vessels the owner has looked at well must be announced, and the גמרא explains the word בדי. The same ברייתא says that items saved from wild animals or floods, or found in crowded places, belong to the finder, because the owner gives up hope (יאוש). The גמרא asks a chain of questions: does this rule apply even where most people are Jews, do the רבנן argue, and how does the הלכה go? It tries to answer from a ברייתא about coins found in בתי כנסיות and from a משנה about a city with Jews and גויים. Both proofs are pushed off, the last one with רב פפא's case of a garbage heap that is about to be cleared.

steps.title: The third item: one's host
steps.stepSummary: This completes שמואל's list (begun on the previous דף) of three things where a תלמיד חכם may change his words. The third is his host (אושפיזא).
steps.simpleTranslation: And with regard to a host.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list from the previous דף: a תלמיד חכם may change his words about his learning, his bed, and here, his host.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About his host, a תלמיד חכם may say he wasn't treated well. This protects a generous host from being swamped by guests. It is the last of three allowed changes, and the next step asks why the list matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Host; the place where a guest stays

phrases.english: And with regard to a host.
phrases.notes: This is the last of three items listed on the previous דף: a scholar's learning, his bed, and his host.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list from the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may change his words regarding his host.

steps.title: Why does this list matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the list of three permitted changes makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we need to know these three cases. It is setting up מר זוטרא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing when a scholar may bend the truth sounds like trivia. The גמרא wants a real case where this knowledge changes the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the purpose of the list just completed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical halachic result that depends on knowing the three permitted changes

steps.title: Returning a lost item by recognition
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא answers that it matters for returning a lost item to a תלמיד חכם who claims it by recognition alone (טביעות עין), without giving signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: it matters for returning a lost item to him based on his recognizing it. If we know he only changes his words in these three things, we return it to him. But if he changes his words in other matters, we do not return it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives the practical result. A scholar known to bend the truth only in these three ways is trusted to claim a lost item by recognition. One who bends the truth in other ways is not trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you must give signs (סימנים) to get a lost item back. A truly honest תלמיד חכם is trusted just by saying 'I recognize it.' The three allowed changes don't count against his honesty, but any other lie does.

keyTerms.meaning: Recognizing an item by sight, without describing signs
A lost item
Changes his words; deviates from the exact truth
We return (the item)

steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם who bends the truth only about his learning, his bed, or his host is still trusted to claim a lost item by recognition. Any other lie loses him that trust.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
For returning to him a lost item based on visual recognition.
If we know about him that he does not alter his words
except in these three things, we return it to him,
but if he alters his words in other matters,
we do not return it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of practical difference
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is in returning a lost item to a תלמיד חכם based on טביעות עין: trusted only if he bends the truth in no other matters.

steps.title: מר זוטרא חסידא and the stolen silver cup
steps.stepSummary: A silver cup was stolen from מר זוטרא חסידא's host. He saw a student dry his hands on a friend's cloak and concluded that this careless student was the thief. He tied him up, and the student confessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A silver cup was stolen from מר זוטרא חסידא's host. He saw a certain student who washed his hands and dried them on his friend's cloak. He said: this is the one who doesn't care about his friend's property. He tied him up, and the student confessed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where מר זוטרא figures out who stole a cup by watching how a student treats other people's things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drying your hands on someone else's cloak without asking shows you don't care about their property. מר זוטרא took this small act as a sign of the student's character. The confession proved him right. Like the previous step, it shows that a person's behavior tells us how far to trust him.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver cup
A student of the study hall
He tied him up
He confessed

phrases.english: Mar Zutra the pious,
a silver cup was stolen from him at his host's place.
He saw a certain student
who washed his hands and dried them on his friend's cloak.
He said: this is the one
who doesn't care about his friend's property.
He tied him up, and he confessed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא חֲסִידָא אִגְּנִיב לֵיהּ כָּסָא דְכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related story about מר זוטרא judging character
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who is careless with others' property can be suspected of dishonesty with it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees about well-seen new vessels
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who lets a finder keep certain new vessels, agrees that new vessels the owner has looked at well must be announced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees that for new vessels that the eye has looked at enough, the finder must announce them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of found vessels and quotes a ברייתא. It shows where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees that a finder must announce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר held (on the previous דף) that a finder need not announce new vessels. Here we learn the limit. If the owner has already looked at them well, he can recognize them, so they must be announced.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees; concedes
That the eye has looked at enough (so the owner recognizes them)
To announce a found item

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar agrees
regarding new vessels that the eye has seen enough,
that he is obligated to announce.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the discussion of found vessels
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New vessels the owner has looked at well must be announced, even according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: Examples of vessels not yet looked at enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists new vessels the owner has not looked at enough, which need not be announced: needles on holders, spinning tools, and strings of axes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are new vessels that the eye has not looked at enough, which one need not announce: for example, holders of needles, spinning tools, and strings of axes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives examples of the opposite case: new items the owner hasn't looked at well, which the finder may keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Items like these come in bulk, freshly bought. The owner hasn't studied them enough to recognize them, so there is no point announcing. The finder may keep them.

keyTerms.meaning: Branches or holders on which needles hang
Spinning tools
Strings of axes

phrases.english: And these are new vessels
that the eye has not seen enough,
which he is not obligated to announce:
for example, branches of needles, and spinning tools,
and strings of axes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן כֵּלִים חֲדָשִׁים שֶׁלֹּא שְׂבָעָתַן הָעַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting category with examples
steps.mimraCoreRuling: New items the owner has not looked at enough, such as needles on holders, spinning tools and strings of axes, need not be announced.

steps.title: Only when found one at a time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the leniency. The finder may keep these items only if he found them one at a time. If he found them two at a time, he must announce.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these that they mentioned, when may one keep them? When he found them one by one. But if he found them two by two, he must announce.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit: the finder may keep these items only if he found them separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single item from a bulk batch gives the owner nothing to identify. When items are found in pairs, the way they were grouped can serve as an identifying detail, so the finder must announce.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted (for the finder to keep)
One at a time; singly
Two at a time; in pairs

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires announcing new vessels the owner looked at well. Bulk new items may be kept, but only when found singly, not in pairs.

phrases.english: All these that they mentioned, when are they permitted?
When he found them one by one,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְצָאָן שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם – חַיָּיב לְהַכְרִיז.
phrases.english: but if he found them two by two, he is obligated to announce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the leniency just given
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The items may be kept only if found one at a time; if found in pairs, they must be announced.

steps.title: What does בדי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word בדי in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'badei'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain a hard word from the ברייתא. It is setting up the definition in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בדי מחטין is unclear. The גמרא wants to know what object the ברייתא is describing.

keyTerms.meaning: The word being defined (from בדי מחטין)

phrases.english: What is 'badei'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the ברייתא

steps.title: בדי means branches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בדי means branches (שוכי).
steps.simpleTranslation: Branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines בדי as branches, the holders the needles hang on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So בדי מחטין are needles hanging on branches. The next step asks why branches are called by this name.

keyTerms.meaning: Branches

phrases.english: Branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question

steps.title: Why call branches בדי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא uses the word בדי for branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call it 'badei'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the name. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual word is שוכי, so the גמרא asks why the ברייתא chose a different word.

keyTerms.meaning: They call it

phrases.english: And why do they call it 'badei'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the definition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the word בדי is used

steps.title: Anything things hang on is called בד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that any object that something hangs on is called a בד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something on which things are hung is called a 'bad'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that בד is the name for anything things hang from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Needles hang on the branch, so the branch is called a בד. The word describes what the object does, not just what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Something on which things hang; a branch
That things are hung on it

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר דְּתָלוּ בֵּיהּ מִידֵּי, ״בַּד״ קָרוּ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: A thing on which something is hung, they call it a 'bad'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the word is used
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Anything on which something hangs is called a בד.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה about ערבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports this meaning of בד from a משנה elsewhere: 'one leaf on one branch.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that which we learned there: one leaf on one branch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from a משנה in סוכה where בד clearly means a branch that a leaf hangs on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the leaf hangs on the בד. This shows the word is used for something that holds things hanging on it, which fits the needles in our ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: That we learned there (in a משנה elsewhere)
Leaf

steps.whatToRemember: בדי מחטין are branches that needles hang on. A בד is anything things hang from, as in the משנה 'one leaf on one branch.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַהוּא דִּתְנַן הָתָם: עָלֶה אֶחָד בְּבַד אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Like that which we learned there: one leaf on one branch.
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה in סוכה, talking about a ערבה with only a few leaves left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the definition with a source
steps.raayaObject: That בד means a branch on which something hangs
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in סוכה: עלה אחד בבד אחד

steps.title: Items saved from danger or found in crowded places belong to the finder
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: an item rescued from a wild animal, the sea or a flooding river, or found in a main road, big plaza or any crowded place, belongs to the finder, because the owner gives up hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר used to say: someone who rescues an item from a lion, a bear, a leopard or a cheetah, or from the tide of the sea or a flooding river, and someone who finds an item on a main road, in a large plaza, or anywhere many people pass, may keep it, because the owners give up hope of getting it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next part of the ברייתא, a new rule from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about when a finder may keep a lost item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All these cases share one idea. The owner is sure the item is gone, either destroyed by danger or picked up by one of the many people passing by. Once the owner has יאוש, the item becomes ownerless and the finder may keep it.

keyTerms.meaning: one who rescues or saves something
the tide or flood of the sea
the overflow or flooding of a river
a main road or highway
a large open plaza
they give up hope (יאוש) of getting the item back

steps.whyThisMatters: The last case, 'any place where many people are found', is what the גמרא is about to question in detail.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And likewise, Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would say:
One who rescues an item from a lion or from a bear
or from a leopard or from a cheetah
or from the tide of the sea
or from the flooding of a river;
one who finds an item on a main road or in a large plaza,
or in any place where many people are found,
these items are his,
because the owners give up hope of getting them back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the word בדי to the next ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items rescued from danger or found in heavily crowded places belong to the finder, because the owner has יאוש.

steps.title: Does the rule apply only where most people are not Jewish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's crowded-place rule applies only where most people are גויים, or even where most are Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: when רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said this, did he mean only a place where most people are גויים, but not a place where most are Jews? Or perhaps he meant even a place where most are Jews?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an open question about how far the 'crowded place' rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where most people are גויים, the owner assumes the finder will not return the item, so he surely gives up hope. Where most are Jews, he might hope a Jewish finder will return it, so maybe he does not give up hope. The question is whether רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule covers that second case too.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised among the חכמים (an open question)
a place where most people are not Jewish
a place where most people are Jews
or perhaps

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: When Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said this,
phrases.notes: He means the last case: an item found where many people pass.

phrases.english: did he mean where most people are not Jewish,
but where most are Jews, not,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אֲפִילּוּ בְּרוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי אָמַר?
phrases.english: or perhaps even where most are Jews he also said so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the scope of the rule just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the crowded-place rule applies even where most people are Jews, who might return the item.

steps.title: If the rule covers a Jewish majority, do the רבנן disagree?
steps.stepSummary: Building on the first question, the גמרא asks: if רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies his rule even where most are Jews, do the רבנן argue with him?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that he applies it even where most are Jews, do the רבנן disagree with him or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question that only arises if the first is answered a certain way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the owner gives up hope even among a Jewish majority is a bold position. So the גמרא asks whether the רבנן accept it or argue with it.

keyTerms.meaning: if you will say (assuming one side of the earlier question)
they disagree
the חכמים, the majority opinion

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. Each question builds on one possible answer to the question before it, like a ladder.

phrases.english: If you will say
that even where most are Jews he also said so,
do the Rabbis disagree with him,
or do they not disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר אֲפִילּוּ בְּרוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the broader answer to step 14 and asks a follow-up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן dispute רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ruling where most people are Jews.

steps.title: If the רבנן disagree, do they disagree even where most are not Jewish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a third question: if the רבנן disagree, they surely do where most are Jews. Do they also disagree where most are גויים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say they disagree: where most are Jews they certainly disagree. Where most are גויים, do they disagree or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its chain of questions by asking how far the רבנן's disagreement reaches. Two more questions follow in steps 17 and 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the רבנן disagree at all, it is clearly in the Jewish-majority case, where the owner has the most reason for hope. The real question is the גוי-majority case, where the owner has little reason for hope. Perhaps the רבנן agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר there.

keyTerms.meaning: certainly, without doubt
they do not disagree

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three linked questions. (1) Does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule cover a Jewish majority? (2) If so, do the רבנן argue? (3) If they argue, do they argue even about a גוי majority? Two more follow in the next steps. The key factor is whether the owner has reason to hope his item will be returned.

phrases.english: And if you will say that they disagree,
where most are Jews they certainly disagree;

phrases.aramaic: בְּרוֹב גּוֹיִם פְּלִיגִי אוֹ לָא פְּלִיגִי?
phrases.english: where most are not Jewish, do they disagree or do they not disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the רבנן disagree (from step 15) and asks how far that disagreement reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן's disagreement also covers places where most people are גויים.

steps.title: Fourth question: Is the הלכה like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: If the רבנן argue with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most are גויים, the גמרא asks whether the הלכה follows him or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say they argue even where most people are גויים, is the הלכה like him, or is the הלכה not like him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another question to its chain. Assuming the רבנן argue with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in every case, it now asks whose side the הלכה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each question builds on the answer to the one before it. The earlier questions asked what each side holds. This one moves to the practical question: which opinion do we actually follow?

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (if it turns out that). It assumes one answer and builds the next question on it.
They argue / disagree
The practical law follows his opinion

phrases.english: And if you will say
that they argue even where most are gentiles
phrases.notes: "They" means the רבנן, who argue with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: is the halacha like him
or is the halacha not like him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר פְּלִיגִי אֲפִילּוּ בְּרוֹב גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the third question (step 16) by assuming the רבנן argue even where most are גויים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר or the רבנן.

steps.title: Fifth question: If the הלכה follows him, how far does it reach?
steps.stepSummary: If the הלכה is like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, does that apply only where most are גויים, or even where most are Jews?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you will say the הלכה is like him, is that only where most are גויים, or even where most are Jews?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last question in the chain. Assuming we follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the גמרא asks whether we follow him only where most are גויים, or also where most are Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה might follow him only in the easier case, where most people are גויים and the owner surely gives up hope. Or it might follow him fully, even where most are Jews. This sets up the proof attempt that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Specifically / only
A place where most people are Jews

steps.whatToRemember: There are five questions in a chain: (1) does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule apply even where most are Jews? (2) do the רבנן argue? (3) do they argue even where most are גויים? (4) is the הלכה like him? (5) if so, even where most are Jews?

phrases.english: If you will say the halacha is like him,
is it only where most are gentiles
or even where most are Jews?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 17 by assuming the answer is that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in practice applies only where most are גויים or also where most are Jews.

steps.title: Proof attempt from coins found in a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says coins found in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות belong to the finder. That fits רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and since those places are Jewish, it would show he applies his rule even where most are Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who finds coins in synagogues, study halls, or any place where many people gather may keep them, because the owner gives up hope. Who do we know follows the crowd? רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. So learn from here that he holds this even where most are Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the very first question in the chain (step 14). It argues that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and is talking about a Jewish place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the reason of 'crowded place', and that is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's reason. A בית כנסת or בית מדרש is full of Jews, so if the finder keeps the coins there, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule must work even where most are Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Synagogues
They give up hope (יאוש) of getting it back
Goes after the many (here: gives weight to a crowded place)
Learn from it / conclude from this

steps.confusionAlert: Here "רוּבָּא" means "the crowd" (a crowded place). It does not mean "majority of גויים" or "majority of Jews."

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who finds coins in synagogues
and in study halls,
and in any place where many people are found –
these belong to him,
because the owners give up hope of them.
Who have you heard
who goes after the crowd?
phrases.notes: He means: who says a crowded place makes the owner give up hope?

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
learn from this
that even where most are Jews too.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַמּוֹצֵא מָעוֹת בְּבָתֵּי כְנֵסִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the questions, the גמרא tries to answer the first one (step 14) from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies his crowded-place rule even where most are Jews.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: coins found in synagogues, study halls, or crowded places belong to the finder, because the owner gives up hope.

steps.title: Rejection: The coins were scattered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The ברייתא is talking about scattered coins, so the crowded-place reason is not what lets the finder keep them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? Scattered coins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by placing the ברייתא in a special case, where the coins were found scattered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scattered coins have no sign by which the owner could identify them, so a finder may keep them anyway. If that is the reason here, the ברייתא proves nothing about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule in a place where most are Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? It introduces a narrower reading of a source.
Scattered (coins lying loose, with no identifying sign)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With scattered coins.
phrases.notes: Scattered coins have no identifying sign, so the finder keeps them no matter where they were found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 19 by reading the ברייתא as a case of scattered coins.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not decide what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר actually holds.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could rest on the coins being scattered (no identifying sign), not on the crowded-place reason.

steps.title: Challenge: Then why mention a crowded place?
steps.stepSummary: If the coins were scattered, the finder would keep them even in an empty place. So why does the ברייתא say 'a place where many people are found'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about scattered coins, why speak of a place where many people are found? Even where many people are not found, the finder keeps them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection it just gave. The scattered-coins reading makes the ברייתא's words about a crowded place seem pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scattered coins belong to the finder in any place. If the ברייתא still bothers to say 'a crowded place', it seems the crowd is part of the reason. That points back to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? It asks why a detail was mentioned if the law would be the same without it.

phrases.english: If it is with scattered coins,
why specifically
a place where many people are found?
Even where many people are not found there!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בִּמְפוּזָּרִין מַאי אִרְיָא מָקוֹם שֶׁהָרַבִּים מְצוּיִין שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of step 20 by showing it makes a detail of the ברייתא unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about scattered coins (step 20).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scattered coins belong to the finder anywhere, so the ברייתא would not need to say 'a crowded place'. Since it does say it, the crowd must matter.

steps.title: The coins were bundled, and the place belonged to גויים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from Step 21. The ברייתא is about bundled coins after all, but the place was a gentile house of assembly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא really is talking about bundled coins. The case is gentile houses of assembly, not our synagogues.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'scattered coins' answer and goes back to bundled coins. It says the 'בתי כנסיות' in the ברייתא are gentile meeting houses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bundled coins normally have a sign, so the finder should announce them. The finder keeps them here because of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's crowded-place reason. Since the place is full of גויים, the ברייתא no longer proves that he applies his rule where most are Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: Bundled or tied-up coins, which can be identified
'And with what are we dealing here?' The גמרא is about to narrow the case
Houses of assembly belonging to גויים

phrases.english: Rather, actually it is about bundled coins,
and with what are we dealing here?
With houses of assembly of gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 21 by returning to bundled coins and moving the case to a gentile place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about Jewish synagogues, so רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies his rule even where most are Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: The place was gentile, so the ברייתא tells us nothing about places where most are Jews.

steps.title: But study halls are only Jewish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: gentile houses of assembly works for בתי כנסיות, but what about בתי מדרשות, which only Jews use?
steps.simpleTranslation: What can you say about the study halls?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The ברייתא also mentions בתי מדרשות, and there is no such thing as a gentile study hall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gentile-place answer only covered half of the ברייתא. Study halls seem to be Jewish places, so the proof that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies his rule where most are Jews seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: Study halls, places where Torah is learned
'What is there to say?' A way of saying the answer does not fit this case

phrases.english: Study halls:
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 22's answer because it does not cover the second place in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about gentile places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Study halls are only Jewish, so the gentile-place answer cannot explain them.

steps.title: Our study halls with גויים sitting in them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the study halls are Jewish ones where גויים are sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means our study halls in which gentiles sit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about study halls. They are Jewish study halls, but גויים are sitting there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is who is in the room, not who owns the building. If גויים are there, the owner gives up hope, so this case is still a 'most are גויים' situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Ours, belonging to Jews
Where they sit, people present in the place

phrases.english: Our study halls
in which gentiles sit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת דִּידַן דְּיָתְבִי בְּהוּ גּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Study halls must be fully Jewish places.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are Jewish study halls with גויים present, so the case still counts as mostly גויים.

steps.title: Synagogues can be read the same way
steps.stepSummary: Now that study halls are Jewish places with גויים in them, the synagogues in the ברייתא can be explained the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, the synagogues too can be our synagogues in which gentiles sit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its defense. It gives one explanation that fits both places in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need to say 'gentile houses of assembly' anymore. Both places are Jewish buildings with גויים present. Either way, the ברייתא does not prove that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies his rule where most are Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now that you have come to this.' Using the new answer for the earlier part too
Gentiles (same meaning as גּוֹיִם here)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about coins in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות is about places with גויים present. So it cannot prove that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies his rule where most are Jews.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
the synagogues too are ours,
in which gentiles sit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses Step 24's answer to replace Step 22's explanation of the synagogues.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proof from the ברייתא (Step 19) is fully pushed off.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about a mixed city
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that in a mixed city you must announce a found item if most people are Jews, but not if most are גויים. Read as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, this would show he applies his rule only where most are גויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone found a lost item there, and most are Jews, he must announce it. If most are gentiles, he does not have to. Who holds that we go after the majority? רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. So learn from this: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר only said his rule where most are gentiles, but not where most are Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer the first question in the chain (step 14). It wants to prove that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule works only where most are גויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה pays attention to who is mostly in the place, and that sounds like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Yet it still requires announcing where most are Jews. That would mean his 'owner gives up hope' rule is limited to places where most are גויים.

keyTerms.meaning: Required to announce the found item
We go after the majority (or the crowd)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he found a lost item in it,
phrases.notes: 'In it' means in a city where both Jews and גויים live.

phrases.english: if most are Jews, he must announce it;

phrases.aramaic: אִם רוֹב גּוֹיִם – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב לְהַכְרִיז.
phrases.english: if most are gentiles, he does not have to announce it.
Whom have you heard
saying that we go after the majority?
phrases.notes: He means the one who cares about the crowd in the place, as in 'a place where many people are found'.

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
Learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר בְּרוֹב גּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: when רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said his rule, it was where most are gentiles,
but where most are Jews, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא proof was pushed off, a new proof is brought for the same first question (Step 14).
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule applies only where most are גויים
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מכשירין about a lost item found in a mixed city

steps.title: The משנה follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? It is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by saying the משנה is the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is not רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, it tells us nothing about how far his rule goes. The 'must announce where most are Jews' line is simply the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose is it?' Asking which תנא a teaching follows

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 26's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה about רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's limits
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It can follow the רבנן.

steps.title: Then the רבנן agree where most are גויים
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is the רבנן, then it proves something else: the רבנן agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר where most are גויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then resolve from it that the רבנן agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר where most are gentiles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the רבנן reading into a proof for the earlier question: do the רבנן argue with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most are גויים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the finder keep the item where most are גויים. If that is the רבנן's view, then they agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in that case. This would answer the third question in the chain (step 16): they do not argue where most are גויים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Resolve from it.' Use this source to answer an open question
They agree with him

phrases.english: Then resolve from it
that the רבנן agree

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר בְּרוֹב גּוֹיִם.
phrases.english: with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר where most are gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes Step 27's reading and uses it to answer the third question (step 16) about whether the רבנן argue where most are גויים.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר where most are גויים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same משנה, read as the רבנן

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and the item was hidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the רבנן reading. The משנה is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who applies his rule even where most are Jews. The 'must announce' case is a hidden item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it really is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and his rule applies even where most are Jews. What case are we dealing with? A hidden item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the last suggestion. It reads the משנה as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר and explains the 'must announce' part as a case where the item was hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hidden item looks like it was put there on purpose, so the owner has not given up hope even in a crowded place. So the 'must announce where most are Jews' line does not limit רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule. The משנה proves nothing about the רבנן either.

keyTerms.meaning: Hidden or buried, an item that looks like it was placed on purpose
Even where most are Jews as well

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא,
phrases.english: Rather, actually it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר,
and his rule applies even where most are Jews too.
And with what are we dealing here? With a hidden item.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 28 by giving a different reading of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both the proof that the רבנן agree (Step 28) and the proof that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is limited (Step 26)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, with the 'must announce' case explained as a hidden item.

steps.title: A hidden item should not be touched at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the hidden-item answer. A hidden item should be left where it is, not picked up and announced, as the משנה about a vessel in a garbage heap teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is hidden, what is it doing with him? Didn't we learn: if someone found a vessel in a garbage heap, if it is covered he should not touch it, and if it is uncovered he takes it and announces it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 29. If the item was hidden, the finder should not have picked it up at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the finder must announce, which means he took the item. But the law for a hidden item is to leave it so the owner can come back for it. So 'hidden' does not seem to fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is it doing with him?' Why did the finder take it at all?
Garbage heap
Covered / uncovered

steps.confusionAlert: Being required to announce means the finder already picked the item up. That is why 'hidden' is a problem: a hidden item should be left in its place.

phrases.english: If it is hidden,
what is it doing with him?!
phrases.notes: Why would the finder even have it in his hands? He should have left it alone.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
If one found a vessel in a garbage heap,
if it is covered, he should not touch it;
if it is uncovered, he takes it and announces it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 29's hidden-item explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the 'must announce' case is a hidden item
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hidden item must be left in place (משנה on 25b, covered vessel in a garbage heap). The משנה here has the finder holding it and announcing it.

steps.title: A garbage heap the owner has decided to clear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge using רב פפא's explanation. The case is a garbage heap that is normally never cleared, but the owner has now decided to clear it. So a hidden item there must be picked up and announced.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פפא said elsewhere: we are dealing with a garbage heap that is not usually cleared, but the owner changed his mind and decided to clear it. Here too, the case is a garbage heap that is not usually cleared, but the owner changed his mind and decided to clear it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 30 by borrowing רב פפא's explanation of a different case and applying it to our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a hidden item is left where it is, because the owner will come back for it. But if the owner of the garbage heap is about to clear it, the item will be thrown out with the garbage, so the finder must take it and announce it. That makes the hidden-item answer from step 29 work, so the משנה can still follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most people are Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: A garbage heap or trash pile
Normally gets cleared away
And he changed his mind / reconsidered
Here too: the same explanation fits our case

steps.whatToRemember: The 'must announce' case in the משנה can be a hidden item in a garbage heap that is about to be cleared. So the משנה does not prove that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר limits his rule to a city where most are גויים. The attempted proof does not settle the question.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a hidden item is always left in place. That is the normal rule, but here the heap is about to be cleared, so leaving it would mean it gets thrown away.

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa said:
It is a garbage heap that is not usually cleared,
and the owner changed his mind about it, deciding to clear it.
Here too,
it is a garbage heap that is not usually cleared,
and the owner changed his mind about it, deciding to clear it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30 by narrowing the hidden-item case to a garbage heap that is about to be cleared.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא), using an earlier explanation by רב פפא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A hidden item should always be left in place, so the משנה's 'must announce' cannot be about a hidden item.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a garbage heap the owner has now decided to clear, a hidden item must be taken and announced. So the hidden-item reading of the משנה stands, and the משנה can follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר even where most are Jews.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה about a mixed city gives no proof about how far רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's rule reaches.
